newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Scramble for S.African gold stocks as bullion lifts.
newsitem.headline: Scramble for S.African gold stocks as bullion lifts.

text.p: A scramble for South African gold shares ensued during the afternoon as the bullion price rose from three-year lows touched on Tuesday and as the rand weakened almost one cent.

Dealers said there was strong local and foreign interest in gold stocks, helped by perceptions that recent sales, which on Tuesday saw the index fall to its lowest level in 11 months, had been overdone.
The gold index added 1.6 percent or 24.1 points to 1,516.5.
Traders said gold shares were seen continuing firmer on Thursday especially if bullion was able to hold its current $371 level.
Industrial shares ended weak for the third consecutive day on Wednesday amid a general lack of direction and a softer rand which ended the day at 4.66 against the dollar.
Dealers said a 79-point overnight loss on Wall Street, its biggest fall since July, had initially hindered stocks.
However, others said the South African market had not looked to the U.S. market for direction for many months. They blamed the 23.1 point fall in the index to 7,968.6 on a lack of direction.
The overall market index was 14.1 points firmer at 6,713.6.
